short: Cascaded decoding with the pretrained encoder is a strong standard result; the end-to-end audio-LLM path beats the prior end-to-end entry but trails RNN cascades, and the cross-species gain is small.
position: The cascaded result holds: the new encoder gives the lowest non-ensembled WER on both Brain-to-Text holdouts with the field's usual 5-gram plus LLM-rescoring decoder. The end-to-end audio-LLM decoder improves on the prior end-to-end entry (15.67% against 24.69% as single models) but is behind the field's cascades on the same data and behind a concurrent Whisper-based end-to-end decoder; the abstract's headline gain sets an LLM-merged ensemble against a non-ensembled entry. Monkey data add little over human pretraining, with no seeds reported. Pretraining can include the benchmark holdout recordings, and removing the fine-tuning participants' data from pretraining raises cascaded WER by 7-14% relative.
